description.narrative:
Pillar 1: Investing in Institutional Strengthening Immediate outcome 1: Nexus members have integrated Enterprise Resource Planning systems for HR, finance, logistics and procurement contributing to financial accountability for efficient and effective, locally-leddelivery of programming.
This project will strengthen institutional capacity of NEXUS members by investing in organizations’ digital ERP, integrating finance, human resources and logistics systems. Starting from a review and audit of NEXUS member organizations’ systems, each NEXUS member will be able to invest in the required upgrade as per identified gaps. Strengthened systems are a key component of institutional capacity, improving financial accountability and allowing for stronger qualitycontrol checks, increased absorption capacity, high-quality project implementation and timely reporting. A total investment of EUR 583,000 for eight organizationsover 4 years, co-funded by the Embassy of The Netherlands and Swiss Development Corporation(SDC), complements current organizational development interventions under DRA. This total amount is calculated based on an amount of EUR 70,000 per organization (based on the average the NEXUS members received from their suppliers after consulting them). The exact amount needed per organization will bedetermined after completion of the system’s audit. Pillar 2: Community-Driven Development with Government and Private Sector Partners Immediate outcome 2: Nexus members have a tested approach for community-driven development with government and private sector partners. The Community-Driven Development (CDD) model supports community-prioritized interventions to improve livelihoods and build demand and capacity for local level development at community level. NEXUS’ locally-led CDD model is unique in its triple nexus approach, integrating humanitarian, development and peacebuilding interventions. As part of the proposed project, NEXUS will undertake three pilot CDD projects in Jubaland (Afmadow District), Galmudug (Adado District) and Somaliland (El Af Weyn District). These are locations where NEXUS members have existing presence. The CDD process and projects will be implemented over the course of 4 years, at acost of EUR 863,705.

participating-org.narrative: It is a Somali women non-governmental humanitarian organization at a national level founded in 1992 at Mogadishu - the capital city, by a group of Somali women intellectuals from cross-section of the community. The Save Somali Women and Children (SSWC) contributeto the creation of a safe and sustainable situation by supporting women to overcome marginalization, violence and poverty in their communities. It operates as a non-profit making organization that has the right to network with a variety of organizations that share similar values and vision. In Somalia women face a range of complex challenges that require multiple solutions. We work in the belief that women through their own efforts and in collaboration with local, national and international allies are central to transforming their own lives and the lives of their communities and population of which they are part. SSWC is women-led and women-centered organization (so its programs reflect the needs of those served) that have well functioning management, finance and programmatic structures and systems.
